learn.hook: If you could fly around the Earth, you would cross seven great landmasses and five vast oceans. Where does India fit in?
points: The large landmasses of the Earth are called continents. There are seven: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.
Asia is the largest continent, and it has the most people. India is in South Asia. Australia is the smallest continent.
Africa is the only continent crossed by the Equator, the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.
Antarctica, around the South Pole, is covered by a thick ice sheet and has no permanent residents, only scientists at research stations. India runs research stations there called Maitri and Bharati.
There are five oceans: the Pacific (the largest and deepest), the Atlantic, the Indian, the Southern and the Arctic (the smallest). The Indian Ocean is the only ocean named after a country.

example.q: Think it through: A ship sails from Mumbai to the east coast of Africa. Which ocean does it cross?
steps: Mumbai is on India's west coast, on the Arabian Sea.
The Arabian Sea is part of the Indian Ocean.
East Africa's coast also faces the Indian Ocean.
So the ship stays in the Indian Ocean all the way.

learn.reallife: Indian ships carry goods across the Indian Ocean, and Indian scientists travel every year to Maitri and Bharati in Antarctica.

topics.title: Grasslands and natural regions of the world

learn.hook: The same kind of grassy plain has different names on every continent: Prairies, Pampas, Steppes, Veld, Downs and Savanna!
points: Places with similar climate, plants and animals form natural regions, such as hot deserts, tropical rainforests, grasslands and polar regions.
Tropical grasslands with tall grass and scattered trees are called savannas. The African savanna is home to lions, zebras, giraffes and elephants.
Temperate grasslands have different local names: Prairies in North America, Pampas in South America, Steppes in Europe and Asia, Veld in South Africa and Downs in Australia.
Temperate grasslands are among the world's great farming regions, growing wheat, maize and other crops and supporting large-scale cattle and sheep rearing.
In cold polar lands near the Arctic, the tundra has only mosses, lichens and small shrubs because the ground stays frozen for most of the year.

example.q: Think it through: Why are the Prairies and the Pampas good for growing wheat?
steps: Both are wide, mostly flat plains.
Their grasses, over thousands of years, made the soil deep and fertile.
They get moderate rainfall, enough for grass and grain crops.
Flat land also makes it easy to use machines for farming.
example.answer: Flat land, fertile soil and moderate rainfall make them ideal for wheat.

learn.reallife: Some of the wheat and pulses traded around the world come from the Prairies of Canada and the Downs of Australia.

topics.title: World landscapes: mountains, deserts, rivers and forests

learn.hook: The world's highest mountain peak, its largest hot desert and its largest rainforest are all on different continents. Let us visit them!
points: The Himalayas, to India's north, are the highest mountain range in the world. Mount Everest, the highest peak on Earth, lies on the border of Nepal and China.
The Andes along the west of South America form the longest mountain range on land. Other great ranges are the Rockies in North America and the Alps in Europe.
The Sahara in northern Africa is the largest hot desert. The Atacama in Chile is one of the driest places on Earth, and the Gobi in Asia is a cold desert.
The Amazon River in South America carries more water than any other river, and the Amazon basin has the largest tropical rainforest. The Nile flows north through Africa into the Mediterranean Sea.
The Great Barrier Reef off north-eastern Australia is the world's largest coral reef system.

example.q: Think it through: Why do very few people live in the middle of the Sahara?
steps: The Sahara gets very little rain.
Days are extremely hot and there is little fresh water.
Without water, crops cannot be grown and animals cannot be kept easily.
So people live mainly near oases and rivers like the Nile.
example.answer: Because there is very little water, people cluster near oases and the Nile instead.

learn.reallife: Mountaineers from India, such as Bachendri Pal, the first Indian woman to climb Everest, have scaled the world's highest peaks.
